no_target_yet.statement:
For every integer $n\geq3$,
\begin{align}
 v(n,1)&=0,\\
 v(n,2)&=\frac4n-\frac8{n^2},\\
 v(n,3)&=\frac8n-\frac{40}{n^2}+\frac{96}{n^3}-\frac{48}{n^4}.
 
\end{align}
The two-draw profile is uniquely maximized at $n=4$, whereas the
three-draw profile is strictly decreasing for $n\geq3$.
The smallest draw count permitting failure of bin-count monotonicity is
$N=2$, since
\[
 v(3,2)=\frac49<\frac12=v(4,2).
\]
The smallest starting draw count permitting failure of sample-size
monotonicity is $N=3$, since $v(n,2)<v(n,3)$ for every $n\geq3$, but
\[
 v(3,4)=\frac{644}{729}<\frac{32}{27}=v(3,3).
\]
no_target_yet.title: Counterexamples to Banić and Elezović's cyclic-dispersion monotonicities

no_target_yet.statement:
For every fixed integer $N\geq2$, there is a polynomial $P_N\in\mathbb Q[q]$
of degree at most $2N-2$ such that $v(n,N)=P_N(1/n)$ for every integer
$n\geq4$. As $q\to0$, its first terms are
\begin{equation}
 P_N(q)=4(N-1)q-4(N-1)(3N-4)q^2+O_N(q^3).
\end{equation}
Consequently $v(n,N)\to0$ as $n\to\infty$, and both $v(n,N)$ and
$\sigma_c(n,N)$ are strictly decreasing for all sufficiently large $n$.
no_target_yet.title: Counterexamples to Banić and Elezović's cyclic-dispersion monotonicities
